titulo: Irregular pretérito indefinido: Verbs with a new stem: tuve, estuve, pude, puse, supe, quise, vine

aula.objetivo: Use the most frequent irregular verbs in the pretérito indefinido: «ser» and «ir» (fui), «dar», «ver», «hacer», the new-stem verbs («tuve, estuve, pude, puse, supe, quise, vine»), «decir» and «traer» (dijeron, trajeron), and verbs like «pedir» and «dormir» (pidió, durmió).

sessao.titulo: Verbs with a new stem: tuve, estuve, pude, puse, supe, quise, vine

blocos.titulo: New stems: tener, estar, poder, poner, saber, querer, venir
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: a group of verbs changes its entire stem in the indefinido and uses its own set of endings: -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -isteis, -ieron. STEP 2: none of these endings carries a written accent. Compare «hablé / habló» (regular, with an accent) and «tuve / tuvo» (irregular, with no accent). STEP 3: the stems to memorize: tener → tuv-, estar → estuv-, poder → pud-, poner → pus-, saber → sup-, querer → quis-, venir → vin-, hacer → hic- (from the earlier section). STEP 4: a full example: «tener»: tuve, tuviste, tuvo, tuvimos, tuvisteis, tuvieron. «Venir»: vine, viniste, vino, vinimos, vinisteis, vinieron. STEP 5: «estar» in the indefinido says where you were during a closed period: «Estuve en Lima una semana» (I was in Lima for a week). STEP 6: some of these verbs shift meaning in the indefinido, because the fact is a single point in time rather than an ongoing state. «Supe la noticia» means «I found out the news» (at that moment), not «I knew». «Pude venir» means «I managed to come», and «No pude venir» means «I wasn't able to come». «No quise venir» means «I refused to come», with the sense of actively declining. «Conocí a Ana» means «I met Ana (for the first time)», and «conocer» is actually regular in this tense. STEP 7: «tener que + infinitive» (lesson 13) in the past also uses the indefinido: «Tuve que trabajar el sábado». STEP 8: watch the «v»: «estuve» and «tuve» both have a «v», and so does «vine». «Estube» and «tubo» (which is actually the word for a pipe) are both mistakes.
blocos.comparacao: English has the same kind of irregular stem-swap in its own past tense — «go/went», «see/saw», «have/had» are just as unpredictable — so the habit of memorizing an irregular form as a whole word, rather than deriving it, transfers directly. What doesn't transfer is the meaning shift some of these verbs carry in Spanish: English «I knew» and «I could» describe ongoing states, with no separate form for a single, pinpoint moment the way Spanish «supe» (I found out, right then) and «pude» (I managed to, on that occasion) do. That's a real distinction to learn, not just a vocabulary item.

exemplos.ru: El jueves tuve un examen difícil.
exemplos.pt: On Thursday I had a hard exam.
We stayed in Lisbon for a week.

exemplos.ru: Ayer supe la noticia por una amiga.
exemplos.pt: Yesterday I found out the news from a friend.

exemplos.ru: No pude ir a la fiesta.
exemplos.pt: I wasn't able to go to the party.

erros.motivo: The stem of «tener» in the indefinido is «tuv-».
These irregular forms carry no accent.

erros.errado: [misto] Ayer él viniró a mi casa.
erros.certo: [misto] Ayer él vino a mi casa.
erros.motivo: The third-person singular of «venir» is «vino», with no accent.
The stem of «saber» in the indefinido is «sup-».

blocos.enunciado: Narrate out loud, in at least eight sentences, the last time you had a commitment: an exam, a meeting, or a party. Use «tuve que», «estuve», «pude», «no pude», «vine», and «supe».
Conjugate «ir» and «hacer» in the indefinido, from «yo» to «ellos». Then say what you saw and what you did yesterday.
